claims.text: The ability to form a homogeneous, self-healing passive oxide film governs high-entropy-alloy resistance to simultaneous wear and corrosion.
Cr and Al are high-passivating components in the proposed high-entropy alloy.
The protective surface film is uniform and rapidly self-heals after mechanical disruption.
The passive film is likely dominated by Cr and/or Al compounds.
Configurational entropy in the high-entropy alloy promotes formation of a dense, chemically homogenized oxide film.
The dense, chemically homogenized oxide film passivates the underlying metal against further corrosive attack.
Mechanical wear disrupts the passive oxide film.
Rapid regeneration of the passive film prevents prolonged or deep exposure of the underlying metal.
Rapid passive-film regeneration limits synergistic wear-corrosion degradation.
Combined wear and corrosion typically accelerate material loss through synergy.
Samples retaining an intact, self-healing passive film will have lower overall mass loss than samples with a compromised passive film during tribocorrosion.
Samples retaining an intact, self-healing passive film will form fewer corrosion pits than samples with a compromised passive film during tribocorrosion.
For film-protected samples, degradation in the combined environment will be less severe than the sum of degradation from isolated wear and isolated corrosion.
The predicted protection should hold when the electrolyte supports passive-film formation and regeneration.
The protective effect should fail when the environment dissolves the oxide faster than it regenerates.
The protective effect should fail when the alloy composition cannot form a continuous passive film.
